purpose: Teach: バリー/メアリー/ラッセル/ジェリー/エド/エドワード/ブラッド/アニー

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがバリー・マニロウのレコードを愛された
lines.en: You remember, dear — when your father was young, he loved that Barry Manilow record.
lines.style: Gentle, reflective pause before the memory. Soft, searching tone as if reaching back decades. Warm but unhurried. Let the memory settle in the pause.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、メアリー・ポピンズの映画を観られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: That's right, dear — and when you were young, you watched Mary Poppins so many times, didn't you?
lines.style: Bright, knowing smile in the voice. Teasing affection — she's turning his gaze back to him. Quick, playful energy. The slight rise on the question shows she's delighting in catching him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがバートランド・ラッセルの著作を蔵書された
lines.en: Gran, your father — when he was young, he had all of Bertrand Russell's works in his study.
lines.style: The same distant, gentle register. A slight wonder in his voice — not quite admiration, more like quiet recognition of a fact that mattered once. Slow cadence. Trailing into the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、トムとジェリーのアニメをお孫様と楽しまれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, dear — when you were young, you used to watch Tom and Jerry with the grandchildren, remember?
lines.style: She's building on his rhythm now, gentle teasing underneath. Her voice bright with the image. A small, knowing laugh at the end of the thought — she's painting him a picture of himself he'd almost forgotten.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがエド・サリヴァンのTVショーを観られた
lines.en: Gran, your father — back then, he never missed Ed Sullivan Show.
lines.style: Quieter this time, almost to himself. The cadence slowing further. A man sifting through layers of time. Voice steady but faded at the edges, like he's speaking from very far away.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、エドワード・ケネディの演説を聴かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, dear — when you were younger, you listened to Edward Kennedy's speeches on the radio, didn't you?
lines.style: Softer now, matching his tone but not his distance. She's not teasing anymore — she's honoring what he's doing. Gentle insistence. A small, private smile. Reaching across time to find him there.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがブラッド・ピットのデビュー作を観られた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he saw Brad Pitt's first film on opening night.
lines.style: Almost a whisper now. The register has shifted — he's very far back in time. Each phrase deliberate, careful. The voice carries the weight of all the years between then and now. A small pause before 'Brad Pitt' — the name like a marker, a place he's trying to reach.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、ミュージカル「アニー」の初演を観られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, love — you saw the premiere of Annie on stage, didn't you? When you were still young.
lines.style: The softest she's been. No teasing now. Just recognition — she knows where he is, and she's meeting him there. Slow, tender, almost a lullaby. The question mark gentle, not prompting but confirming. A hand reaching across decades.
